message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc serves technology innovators as a mission critical design enablement partner, connecting market leading design, emulation and test solutions across the full lifecycle for customers in AI infrastructure, communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor and general electronics [D1]. In the third fiscal quarter ended July 31, 2026, revenue was $1.85 billion, which was 36.54% higher than a year earlier, and net income was $397 million, which was 107.85% higher [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue was $1.35 billion, up 43.09% from the year earlier period, and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.6% [D1]. Commercial communications revenue growth was led by the wireline business, and wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time in the company's history [D2]. Management tied the demand to the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, where design margins are shrinking and test intensity is rising [D4]. Keysight also announced a research collaboration with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York to advance AI safety assurance for software defined vehicles [D7].

Guidance for the quarter in progress is revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1]. The mid-point of the revenue range represents year-over-year growth of approximately 37% [D1]. Management described record results and broad based growth across its markets and said it was raising its outlook for the fourth quarter and for the full fiscal year [D3]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that the pipeline continues to grow strongly [D3]. Management said its base case is that the opportunity in 6G is greater than the opportunity in 5G [D3]. The industry has moved from exploratory research toward funded development programs following the setting of a 2029 standard timeline [D4]. Integration of recent acquisitions, including Spirent, was completed one quarter ahead of schedule [D4]. Most of the cost synergy target is expected to be realized on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3].

Analysts pressed on whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints are limiting guidance, and the call summary described their tone as slightly negative to pressing [D3]. Management said the supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that the supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago [D3]. Management added that revenue conversion is likely to be nonlinear over the next few quarters as external supply dependencies are managed [D4]. The chief financial officer said the one-time tariff impacts this year artificially pulled up 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Within the Communications Solutions Group, cost of products and services rose 25.56% and research and development rose 26.14% [D1]. Segment operating income growth across the reported segments was 81.36% [D1].

The market's valuation debate takes place at a forward price to earnings ratio of 20.66 and a trailing price to earnings ratio of 45.89, against trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D5]. Commentary on the stock argues that AI growth is strong but that the valuation leaves little room for error [D3]. Another piece argues that further stock price gains are unsupported by fundamentals [D3]. The analyst write-up holds that price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide and are often set to drum up interest in shares of companies whose firms have or seek business relationships [D5]. The same write-up notes that the consensus earnings estimate for the current year has increased over the last 30 days, with no negative revision [D5]. The bull case rests on the AI infrastructure build-out continuing to pull wireline and commercial communications demand, while the bear case rests on supply converting that demand into revenue at a non-linear pace and on a profitability comparison that the tariff effects will not repeat [D3].
